title: Through the heavens
hook: he rises through the heavens, meeting Adam, Isa, Yahya, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa and Ibrahim (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Isra: carried by night to Jerusalem, at the front of a row of prophets. Your line was: the prophets in one row.

A gate in the sky, and a voice behind it asking: who is it? Jibril. And who is with you? Muhammad. Has he been sent for? Yes. Then welcome to him; what an excellent visit. And the gate opens. In Sahih al-Bukhari, that short exchange happens again and again, at gate after gate. Muslims tell it as the same night as yesterday's journey: Jerusalem was the first leg. Now he rises. Today's word: Mi'raj, the ascent.
screen: `WHO IS IT?` → `HAS HE BEEN SENT FOR?` → `THE GATE OPENS.`

segments.voice: Mi'raj is the name Muslims give to the ascent. Bukhari's reports, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'a and others, walk through it heaven by heaven, and at each one, someone is waiting. In the first heaven, Adam. Another report in Bukhari, from Abu Dharr, describes figures to his right and to his left: when he looks to the right he laughs, and when he looks to the left he weeps. They are his own descendants, the people of the garden on one side, the people of the fire on the other. In the second heaven, two cousins, Yahya and Isa, John and Jesus. In the third, Yusuf. In the fourth, Idris. In the fifth, Harun, the brother of Musa. In the sixth, Musa himself. And in the seventh, Ibrahim. At each heaven the greeting is nearly the same. Adam and Ibrahim say: welcome, righteous son, righteous prophet. The others say: welcome, righteous brother, righteous prophet. Son, from the fathers. Brother, from the rest. A few days ago, three brothers in Ta'if wouldn't even speak to him. Now every heaven has family in it. Beyond the seventh heaven, the reports describe the lote tree of the furthest boundary, which the Qur'an mentions in surah fifty-three. The Qur'an itself gives few details of the ascent; the details are in the hadith. Some of these names appear in the Bible too, as Adam, John, Jesus, Joseph, Aaron, Moses and Abraham. Here they stand at their stations, waiting to say welcome.
screen: `MI'RAJ: THE ASCENT.` · `ADAM LAUGHS RIGHT, WEEPS LEFT.` · `HEAVEN BY HEAVEN, TO IBRAHIM.` · `WELCOME, SON. WELCOME, BROTHER.` · then, large: `MET AT EVERY HEAVEN.`

segments.voice: If you can, look at the sky through a window or outside; if not, close your eyes and picture it. Then name them in order, one per breath, Adam, Yahya and Isa, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa, Ibrahim, letting one thing you remember about each come up. If you pray, you can send peace on each of them, as Muslims do when they say the prophets' names.
Mi'raj: the ascent. In Bukhari, he rises through the heavens and at each one a prophet greets him, as a son or as a brother. Today's word.
Your line: met at every heaven. Turned away below, welcomed above. Day seven hundred fifty-five, done.

howItsDone: Muslims learn the order of the heavens and the prophets met in each from the hadith of the Mi'raj, and say 'peace be upon him' after a prophet's name.

fork.setup: in the first heaven you see Adam with figures to his right and left. when he looks to the left, what does he do?
fork.reveal: Abu Dharr's report in Bukhari: he laughs looking right and weeps looking left; both sides are his descendants.

original.note: Arabic: the ascent; the name given to this part of the night journey.

trapdoor: what you thought: a flight into the sky.
what it means: a rising through the heavens, greeted at each by a prophet as son or brother.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari's reports from Malik ibn Sa'sa'a and Abu Dharr; the gate dialogue; the lote tree of 53:14.
recall: his wife, the one he ran home to

chat.says: What's the Mi'raj? Is it the same as the trip to Jerusalem?
options: No, it's the ascent after it; a prophet greets him at each heaven.
Yes, Mi'raj is just another name for the ride to Jerusalem.
No, it's his climb up Mount Hira to receive the first verses.
chat.meaning: Muslims tell it as the same night: Jerusalem first, then the ascent. In Bukhari, a prophet greets him at each heaven, as son or brother.

Idris.meaning: the prophet in the fourth heaven

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3207 (Malik ibn Sa'sa'a: the gates, 'who is it? has he been sent for?'; Adam, Yahya and Isa, Yusuf, Idris, Harun, Musa, Ibrahim; the greetings)
Sahih al-Bukhari 349 (Abu Dharr: Adam laughs looking right, weeps looking left)
Qur'an 53:13–16 (the lote tree of the furthest boundary)

notes: Bukhari 3207 and 349 numbers cited from memory; confirm. Abu Dharr's report places some prophets differently from Malik ibn Sa'sa'a's; the script follows the index (Malik's order).
Confirm the greeting forms: 'righteous son' from Adam and Ibrahim, 'righteous brother' from the others.
Root etymology of Mi'raj was left out under the claims rule; a Keeper may add it (ayn-ra-jim, to ascend).
'The Qur'an itself gives few details of the ascent' is a general statement; some scholars read 53:1–18 as referring to it. Confirm phrasing.
The myth item about the gate dialogue tests who is asked; confirm the hadith (the gatekeeper asks Jibril).
Idris was left out of the Bible-names list because the Idris/Enoch identification is debated. In the second heaven, confirm Bukhari calls Yahya and Isa maternal cousins.
